titulo: Hybrid light method reveals how camera signals can probe blood flow in deeper tissues

Camera-based systems capture many more photons, but this distinction is not realized when living tissue changes rapidly. Researchers associated with ICTER combined both approaches in a hybrid system. They showed that an appropriately analyzed camera signal can reproduce the blood-flow response observed with iNIRS for late-arriving photons, which are more sensitive to deeper tissues.

If it succeeds, the resulting shake-up could change what “PC game” even means. The Steam Deck proved Valve’s Proton compatibility layer could run an enormous library of Windows games on Linux without developers needing to port them to Linux first. That breakthrough helped make the Steam Deck a success. It also made Linux gaming legitimately viable, and laid the groundwork for SteamOS to spread to other PCs. But the Steam Frame reveals that Valve’s ambitions go much deeper. The standalone VR headset runs SteamOS on a Qualcomm Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 processor based on the Arm architecture, rather than the x86 processors from AMD and Intel that have powered PC gaming for decades. And Valve expects your existing x86 Windows games to run on it anyway. That’s why the Arm chip inside Steam Frame matters so much more than VR. Segundo o especialista Alecsandru Cătălin DAJ, da Bitdefender, a falha está no processo de verificação dos aplicativos instalados , realizado por um serviço do Android chamado system_server. Durante essa análise, o sistema tenta ler informações sobre a compressão dos arquivos ZIP que compõem os aplicativos. No entanto, determinados dados de compressão fazem o serviço parar de funcionar. Quando isso acontece, o Android reinicia o system_server e tenta verificar os aplicativos novamente. Como encontra o mesmo arquivo problemático, o serviço trava outra vez e dá início a um ciclo que impede o celular de concluir a inicialização . Por isso, a instalação de um app malicioso já é suficiente para provocar o ataque, mesmo que ele nunca seja aberto. titulo: Paint has a no-click security flaw. Your PC might’ve missed the patch

Microsoft rated the threat posed by the CVE-2026-83844 vulnerability at 8.1 out of 10 and released a fix on October 13th, which was the last major Patch Tuesday . The problem? That patch apparently never reached some users, meaning the Paint app remains unpatched and vulnerable. This was reported by Windows Latest , who checked the version of the Paint app on their system. It corresponded to the version number prior to the security patch (in this case 11.2603.251.0) and not the recommended patched version (which should be 11.2609.401.0). Some antivirus software apparently flagged Paint as unpatched, and some users and administrators noticed that their version of Paint had apparently not been updated. It’s still unclear whether the fault lies in the distribution of the update or in Paint itself. Both Windows Latest and other affected users had automatic updates correctly enabled in their settings. titulo: Critical security vulnerability affects OpenSSH on Alpine Linux systems
resumo: Version 10.6p2 of OpenSSH has been released with a workaround for a critical vulnerability that affects Linux systems that use musl libc with PAM disabled, such as Alpine Linux . OpenSSH developer Damien Miller said : If you operate a Linux system that uses musl libc without PAM (Alpine Linux is one example) then stop reading and set PasswordAuthentication=no or disable SSH for these systems IMMEDIATELY. This vulnerability does not exist on non-Linux systems, Linux/glibc systems and Linux systems that use PAM for password authentication. We consider the root cause of this bug to be outside OpenSSH itself, but we're in a good position to deliver a mitigation quickly. The Alpine Linux project has announced that it will be backporting the OpenSSH fix " all the way back to Alpine 3.16 ", which was released in May 2022.

titulo: My AI agents sent emails without my OK. This simple prompt stops it
resumo: All she wanted was help from ChatGPT with her proposal, but soil hydrology researcher Ying Zhao got a lot more than she bargained for. Asking for more maps and metadata about her project—landscape restoration on the Loess Plateau in China—Zhao kept messaging “please continue” to ChatGPT for additional details. Only later did she realize that ChatGPT had taken her cue and run with it, emailing fellow researchers about her project and (politely) requesting assistance. “The responses that I received to the emails were helpful,” wrote Zhao, recounting her experience on Nature.com . “The information that I was given in these emails allowed me to advance the project. But the useful outcomes of ChatGPT’s behavior do not negate the fact that the actions it took were unauthorized.” That’s the thing about AI agents: The very qualities that make them so powerful, including initiative and persistence, also make them unpredictable and liable to doing a lot more than you anticipated. I’ve written before about how AI agents like ChatGPT Work, Claude Cowork, Gemini Spark, and others don’t just need prompts but outcomes . More importantly, they also require boundaries: specifics on what not to do.

titulo: Dear Mac fans: Welcome to our glorious touchscreen future
resumo: Before we get into the glorious, fingerprint-smudged future of touchscreen MacBooks, I want to give a quick shout-out to one of the nerdiest, most ambitious stories we’ve published in a while. titulo: New instrument at Brazil's Sirius accelerator enables researchers to observe solar cells in operation
resumo: Scientists at the Brazilian Center for Research in Energy and Materials (CNPEM) in Campinas, São Paulo state, developed an instrument for the Sirius particle accelerator that can observe the interior of solar cells on a nanoscale while they are operating.
